QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_69

question.text: In assessing financial-inclusion outcomes such as those in the E-Diksha case, the SIA should treat deadweight as follows:

answer.text: Consider other Government and non-Government financial-inclusion efforts that participants may benefit from anyway, and use dead weights so the report avoids overclaiming

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook supports the use of dead weights to avoid overclaiming and notes the relevance of Government scheme and RBI data when assessing attribution. Where other Government or non-Government financial-inclusion efforts could have produced part of the outcome anyway, that contribution is deadweight. The Trap: Participants refusing, moving districts or not being selected are attrition or selection issues, not deadweight. Note: Disclose the basis used to estimate deadweight, including references to relevant Government scheme data and acknowledged attribution limitations.
